punchline: Osage oil income could be inherited but not sold, and the killings began inside exactly that rule.
thirty_sec: In 1920s Oklahoma the Osage were among the richest people per head in the world, because of oil beneath their land. White guardians managed much of their money. Then family members began to die: a body found in a ravine, a house blown up. David Grann says the FBI's new bureau uncovered a plot tied to inheritance, and that the real death toll was higher than the trials showed.
